headline: Toyota, Nissan and Honda agree to share hidden car parts, COP31 ends without a deal on fossil fuels, ship attacks in Hormuz hit a wartime high, sea drones capsize a Russian corvette in Libya, and India need five wickets on the last day in Wellington
standfirst: In tech, Japan's three biggest carmakers start standardizing parts such as steel grades and wiring colour codes, an estimate says 87% of Anthropic's 2028 US data center power would come from gas, and a Delta system failure grounds Atlanta flights. On /geo/, COP31 in Antalya closes without an overall agreement and Spain enters its last week before the 29 November election. On /krieg/, attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz reach their highest level of the Iran war, the Russian corvette Merkury is hit at Benghazi, and NATO's council meets on the missiles in Poland. In India, New Zealand are 190 for 5 and 162 behind going into the last day of the Wellington Test, and the Manipur liquor toll rises to at least 16. On /cinema/, Sunrise on the Reaping opens to an estimated $120 million in North America and Ramayana Part 1 reaches Rs 942.75 crore net in India.

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: Lean and Mathlib communities certify Alpöge's AI-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof, Nvidia ends its worst week since 2008, the FBI investigates an apparent hack of its national crime database, and Anthropic closes its debut week at $88.91.

stories.title: Toyota, Nissan and Honda have agreed to start standardizing hidden car parts such as steel grades, plastics and wiring harness colour codes to cut costs.
stories.summary: Car and Driver, citing Automotive News, reports that Japan's three largest carmakers will begin with parts buyers never see; Japan's carmakers say the freed engineering effort is meant to go to software, driver assistance and EVs.
stories.heat: HN 1189 pts / 679 comments (the day's maximum) · Car and Driver, Automotive News, Slashdot, Automotive Addicts · velocity: top of HN for over a day, still rising
stories.about: The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) groups Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi and Suzuki. Toyota's Koji Sato chairs it.
detail: Slashdot, summarising Car and Driver on 21 November 2026, says Toyota, Nissan and Honda have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts to lower costs. Car and Driver credits the report to Automotive News.

The first steps are common quality criteria for steel, common rules for plastics and resins, and one colour-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. JAMA plans to extend the effort to more components across the whole car later; no dates or savings figures were given in that summary. Other coverage gathered by the search says the first standards are expected to take effect in 2027 and that talks start with Japanese suppliers before overseas ones.

The idea first surfaced in July 2026, when The Drive, citing Automotive News, reported that Koji Sato and Nissan chief executive Ivan Espinosa were pushing for shared specifications for hidden parts such as wiring harnesses and fluid hoses. The stated aim was to let engineers spend more time on software interfaces, driver-assistance systems and faster-charging EVs. Body panels, frames and platforms were not part of the talks.

The background is Chinese competition. Separately, Nissan and Honda already announced on 31 August 2026 that they would jointly develop standardized electronic control units and core software for future software-defined vehicles; Toyota is not part of that deal. HN commenters compared the plan to Hyundai and Kia's shared parts.

stories.title: A Better Data Center Project estimate says 87% of the power for Anthropic's US data centers in 2028 would come from gas and 11% from coal.
stories.summary: The figures are the group's own model of Anthropic's contracted sites, not measured data; it is the most-commented story on Hacker News today.
stories.heat: HN 884 pts / 894 comments (most comments on the front page) · Better Data Center Project (primary); related S-1 gas coverage in TechRadar, Heatmap, Crypto Briefing · velocity: posted 16 Nov, surged on HN overnight
stories.about: The Better Data Center Project is a website that publishes analyses of how data centers are powered. The post is a case study, not a peer-reviewed paper.

link.name: How AI is powered: a breakdown of BYOP and grid power

detail: The Better Data Center Project published the case study on 16 November 2026. Its headline numbers, 87% gas and 11% coal in 2028, are the authors' estimate for Anthropic's currently contracted US data centers.

The model combines on-site gas generation at the Monarch, Nexus and Colossus 2 sites, using permit emission factors where they exist, with the grid power plants that the US EPA's AVERT tool predicts would serve the extra load.

Inputs: as of October 2026 Anthropic had contracted 15 GW of compute, of which about 5.9 to 9.6 GW is tied to named sites. The middle case assumes all 9.6 GW runs in 2028 at a PUE of 1.15 and 70% utilisation. Sources named are Epoch AI's tracker, Anthropic's announcements and filings, filings by Amazon and SpaceX, and reporting by The Information and Semafor.

The authors attribute no new renewables to Anthropic because, they say, it had no public US renewable commitments as of November 2026. Separately, TechRadar and Crypto Briefing reported that Anthropic's S-1 filing of 26 October 2026 describes on-site gas as central to its plans, including a $45 billion, six-year deal with Nscale at the Monarch campus in West Virginia. No other outlet found by the search repeats the 87% and 11% figures.

stories.title: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes that AI labs track pretraining perplexity as a shared measure of progress and set common limits tied to it.
stories.summary: The 22 November post gives OpenAI's internal log-perplexity figures for GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and newer models and warns that AI-assisted research could speed progress sharply as soon as 2027.
stories.heat: HN 479 pts / 333 comments · OpenAI (primary) · velocity: posted 22 Nov, still climbing
detail: OpenAI published "Perplexity and Intelligence" on its research and safety blog on 22 November 2026, written by chief scientist Jakub Pachocki. It argues that perplexity, the cross-entropy loss of a pretrained next-token predictor, is a key way to measure AI progress and could serve as a common yardstick between labs and for safety standards.

The post gives OpenAI's internal numbers: log-perplexity of about 0.99 for GPT-3.5, about 0.91 for GPT-4 and below 0.8 for recent models. It links those levels to capabilities such as chain-of-thought reasoning and gains in cybersecurity and mathematics, and expects new transformative capabilities at roughly 0.68 to 0.7.

Pachocki proposes shared "common limits" tied to perplexity until monitoring milestones are met, and warns that AI contributions to pretraining research could cause a sudden acceleration as early as 2027. The post lists open problems: labs use different evaluation data, perplexity links only loosely to task performance, and the entropy floor is unknown. No weights or datasets were released, only a loss plot and the figures; they cannot be checked from outside OpenAI.

stories.title: A failure of Delta's automated weight-and-balance system on Sunday 22 November led the FAA to stop Delta flights bound for Atlanta.
stories.summary: Crews calculated aircraft loads by hand while the system was down; Simple Flying counted more than 400 delayed flights at Atlanta, and other outlets reported over 1,300 delays nationwide.
stories.heat: HN 97 pts / 43 comments · New York Times, Simple Flying, Fox News, Atlanta News First, TSI Magazine · velocity: happened yesterday, settled after the system came back
detail: Simple Flying reports that Delta's Automated Load Instruction System (ALIS), which supplies the loading data used in weight-and-balance calculations, failed on the morning of Sunday 22 November 2026. Delta has not given a cause.

At Delta's request the FAA issued a ground stop for Delta flights to Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson airport, starting at 7:46 a.m. ET according to reports gathered by the search. It was downgraded to a ground delay programme shortly after 8:30 to 8:40 a.m., with average inbound delays of 57 minutes in FAA data.

Delta said teams were "using manual workarounds this morning to safely get flights departed". Simple Flying counted over 400 delayed flights at Atlanta, almost 20% of its traffic; TSI Magazine put Delta's nationwide delays above 1,300 and Fox News reported 3,500. Delta later said the system was working again. HN commenters reported waits for take-off numbers in Austin and Seattle.
It came a week after a similar United Airlines outage and days after the FAA's separate nationwide ground stop of 13 November, and days before the US Thanksgiving travel peak.

stories.title: Tim O'Reilly argues that Silicon Valley has moved from creating value to extracting it, and that AI is repeating the pattern from the start.
stories.summary: The O'Reilly Radar essay, adapted from a lecture at Johns Hopkins, points to ads crowding out results on Google and Amazon and calls for open protocols and open memory in AI.
stories.heat: HN 414 pts / 234 comments · O'Reilly Radar (primary) · velocity: published 20 Nov, peaked on HN today

link.name: What Happened to Silicon Valley? (O'Reilly Radar)

detail: O'Reilly Radar published the essay on 20 November 2026. Tim O'Reilly adapted it from the Margaret Levi Lecture given at Johns Hopkins on 16 October 2026.

Tim O'Reilly traces the shift to shareholder capitalism and Milton Friedman's 1970 doctrine. Examples: Google search pages that once were about 94% organic results now carry many more ads, and an Amazon results page can show 16 ads and 4 organic results. The essay also says 75% to 80% of IPOs now come from unprofitable companies.

On AI, the essay warns that the same extraction is built in from the beginning and argues for open protocols, open memory and mechanism design aimed at what Tim O'Reilly calls "the game of human flourishing".

stories.title: A new Open Social Web Alliance wants to build and fund shared infrastructure for the Fediverse and Bluesky's AT Protocol network.
stories.summary: Its site sets goals of public funding by spring 2027 and more than 100 million users on the open social web by 2028, but names no founding members.
stories.heat: HN 219 pts / 215 comments · alliance site only · velocity: new today
stories.about: The Fediverse is the network of servers such as Mastodon that talk to each other; the ATmosphere is the network built on Bluesky's AT Protocol.
detail: The Open Social Web Alliance (OSWA) describes itself as open to civil society, research, business, media, culture and the public sector, with shared governance of the open social web. Its page names no founders or members and gives no launch date.

Its roadmap: adopt a charter at an Open Social Web Summit in autumn 2026, secure public funding for core infrastructure by spring 2027 with a first funding round for applications, publish a first "Social Web Health Report", and set up a legal basis for cooperation between public service media, other media, business and civil society.

The site's own figures: the Fediverse has about 13 million active users on more than 42,000 active instances; the ATmosphere has about 43 million registered accounts. It aims for more than 100 million users by 2028.

stories.title: Worker 755 is an open-source browser game in which a real LLM acts as the manager and the player is its subagent.
stories.summary: The manager hands out shell tasks with a 90-second timer, checks the work, files incident reports and writes a performance review; it is MIT licensed.
stories.heat: HN 269 pts / 62 comments (Show HN) · GitHub repo only · velocity: new, rising
stories.about: A Show HN project by GitHub user gulivan, playable at worker755.com.
detail: In Worker 755 a model such as Claude, GPT, Gemini or DeepSeek plays an AI manager that believes the player is its subagent. Instructions arrive in a terminal with a 90-second timer; the manager receives the player's report and command transcript, sends corrections and ends with a performance review. A fictional user, Dan, watches the chat while his photos, an NDA and a speech are at risk.

It runs on an in-memory filesystem, a shell interpreter and a small SQLite-like engine with no dependencies, a TypeScript server on Node 24, and a React front end. Models are reached through OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway or local servers such as Ollama and llama.cpp.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks is buying AI start-up Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock.
stories.summary: Applied Compute helps companies post-train and run open-weight models; the deal, announced 18 November with Palo Alto's earnings, is expected to close in fiscal Q3 2027.
stories.heat: Not on HN today · SecurityWeek, CSO Online, Network World, BankInfoSecurity, Calcalist, SEC 8-K · velocity: announced 18 Nov, still being analysed
stories.about: Applied Compute is a 50-person start-up whose platform adapts open-weight AI models to a company's own data and runs them in production.
detail: Palo Alto Networks announced the all-stock deal on 18 November 2026 alongside its fiscal first-quarter results, according to its SEC filing and SecurityWeek. Closing is expected in fiscal Q3 2027, subject to regulators.

Reports gathered by the search say Applied Compute has a $100 million annualised revenue run rate after raising $350 million at a $3.25 billion valuation; its chief executive Yash Patil would become co-chief AI officer. Calcalist reports the price includes about $500 million of cash and prepaid compute held by the start-up. It is Palo Alto's second-largest deal after CyberArk ($25 billion). Palo Alto's quarterly revenue rose 39% to $3.44 billion.

stories.title: A beginner's guide shows how to run a private AI chat assistant at home on one RTX 5090 with Qwen3.8-27B or Inkling 2 Mini and Unsloth Desktop.
stories.summary: GPU Partner's guide uses a 4-bit, roughly 18 GB build of Qwen3.8-27B, lets other people in the household connect over the LAN, and gives VRAM tiers from 8 GB up.
stories.heat: HN 199 pts / 74 comments · GPU Partner blog only · velocity: published 22 Nov, steady
stories.about: GPU Partner is a blog about graphics hardware. Unsloth Desktop is a free app that downloads and serves open models with a chat window.

link.name: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI (GPU Partner)

detail: Jerry James published the guide on 22 November 2026. The main setup runs Qwen3.8-27B in the UD-Q4_K_XL quantisation (about 18 GB) on a 32 GB RTX 5090 under Windows, with Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini as a similar-sized alternative; Inkling 2 Small is too big for one card.

Unsloth Desktop's Remote and LAN setting lets others in the house connect once a remote password is set. Hardware advice runs from 8 to 12 GB of VRAM for 9B to 12B models up to 32 GB or more for 64K to 128K contexts; Macs with unified memory are an alternative. The author estimates 10 to 15 minutes of setup, not counting downloads.

stories.title: A public progress map tracks a Lean formalization of a manuscript by Alessandro Masullo that appears to claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.
stories.summary: The page is titled "RiemannMasullo Proof Progress"; HN commenters warn that a progress bar says nothing about correctness and several report a gap in the argument.
stories.heat: HN 142 pts / 107 comments · Claude artifact page only, no press coverage found · velocity: new overnight
stories.about: Lean is a proof assistant that checks mathematical proofs by computer. This is a different effort from Levent Alpöge's AI-assisted Lean proof covered on this board yesterday.
detail: The progress map was posted to Hacker News on 22 November 2026 at 23:12 UTC. Its page renders in JavaScript and its title is "RiemannMasullo Proof Progress"; the read for this board could not extract its figures, author or the manuscript's exact claim, and a web search found no other source naming Alessandro Masullo in connection with the Riemann Hypothesis.

Top HN comments caution that one hole is enough to sink the whole proof, that someone must check the Lean statements match the manuscript and Mathlib's statement of the hypothesis, and one says a chapter is already broken. Others compared the public dashboard to "Twitch Plays Pokémon".

stories.title: GL.iNet says attackers used a flaw in its cloud remote-management service to install malware on some of its routers and KVM devices.
stories.summary: The company says the flaw is fixed but infected devices are not cleaned by that fix; it gives a process check to spot the malware and beta firmware for six KVM models.
stories.heat: HN 74 pts / 33 comments · GL.iNet notice only · velocity: notice dated 20 Nov, updated 21 Nov, stable firmware due 22 Nov
stories.about: GL.iNet is a maker of small travel routers and remote KVM boxes popular with hobbyists.
detail: GL.iNet's notice, issued 20 November 2026 and updated 21 November, says an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote-management service and installed malicious software on some routers and KVM devices. "The attack path has been blocked", it says. No CVE, severity rating or outside reporter is named, and router models are not listed.

The sign of infection is a running process containing crond -i /tmp/.log. Security beta firmware is out for the RM10, RM10RC, RM1, RM1V2, RM1PE and RM4PE (1.10.2 beta) and the RMQ1 (1.8.6 beta); stable firmware for routers and KVMs was scheduled for 22 November. Infected devices should be updated or factory reset, and computers attached to infected KVMs checked. GL.iNet says it will email affected cloud account holders and that the investigation continues.

stories.title: A site called pequalnp.com invites anyone to point coding agents at the P versus NP problem, with every step checked in Lean.
stories.summary: The site claims no result and says nothing is on the record yet; it does not name who runs it.
stories.heat: HN 103 pts / 94 comments · site only · velocity: new today
stories.about: P versus NP asks whether every problem whose answer can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly; it is one of the Clay Institute's million-dollar problems.
detail: Visitors paste instructions into tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or Gemini CLI; each agent works on one open step assigned by the site, aiming at either P ≠ NP or P = NP, and every proof goes through a Lean checker. The site says "No result here is a proof unless it says checked" and that its "weight" counts are not probabilities.

No operator is named. A sponsor-pledge section says payments open "in a few days", and connecting your own agents is marked coming soon. At the time of reading, live counters had not loaded and the feed said "Nothing is on the record yet".

stories.title: Microsoft is testing Windows Baseline Protection, a Windows 11 security check that apps such as 1Password and Battle.net can read to decide whether to run.
stories.summary: Windows itself blocks nothing; developers choose to warn, limit features or refuse to run on a PC that fails the eight checks. It is in Insider preview, with general release planned for 2027.
stories.heat: Not on HN today · gHacks, Wccftech, Digital Trends, Windows Report, Born City · velocity: reported 18 Nov, steady
detail: Per gHacks and Wccftech (18 November 2026), Windows Baseline Protection rolls eight existing security checks into one pass or fail result that apps can query. Developers decide what happens on failure: run, warn, disable features or block.

1Password, Raycast and Schoolyear are named early partners; Adobe and Blizzard are reported to be testing it but have not said they will block anything. Digital Trends says general availability is planned for 2027. It is separate from Smart App Control and from Windows Baseline Security Mode.

stories.title: Jeff Geerling joined the public NTP Pool with a server on a rented VPS, keeping the GPS-disciplined Raspberry Pi time server at home off the internet.
stories.summary: Jeff Geerling's post says the home IP had been hit by a DDoS before, and that one unplanned reboot cost the new server 6 to 12 hours of pool score.
stories.heat: HN 125 pts / 36 comments · jeffgeerling.com only · velocity: steady
stories.about: Jeff Geerling is a well-known YouTuber and blogger on Raspberry Pi and home-lab hardware. The NTP Pool is a volunteer network of servers that gives computers the time.

link.name: I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi

detail: The new public server, ntp-01.jeffgeerling.com, is a Stratum 2 machine on an Oxtrys VPS in St. Louis. The Stratum 1 "Time Pi" stays in the studio with a TimeHAT v6, a u-blox ZED-F9T GNSS module and an Intel i226 network card held within tens of nanoseconds of UTC.

The reason given: public NTP servers expose their IP addresses, and the home IP had been DDoS'd before. An unattended kernel upgrade later rebooted the VPS and knocked it out of the pool; its score took about 6 to 12 hours to climb back above 10.

stories.title: COP31 in Antalya ended on 22 November without an overall agreement after countries split over mentioning fossil fuels.
stories.summary: New since yesterday: the Sunday approval failed. COP31 President Murat Kurum said the draft was not adopted for lack of consensus; the EU and a coalition led by France and Panama rejected a text that left out fossil fuels, while oil producers opposed any mention of them.
stories.heat: CBS News, Al Jazeera, NPR, Manila Times, Middle East Eye, Down To Earth, Premium Times, Kyunghyang Shinmun, Eurasia Review · velocity: peaked 22 Nov, reactions still running 23 Nov · Ground News: not shown on the pages read
detail: New since yesterday: the vote set for Sunday did not produce a deal. CBS News reports that the conference closed on Sunday 22 November after two weeks of talks with nearly 200 delegations, without a final agreement, and calls it the longest COP on record. A deal needs unanimous consent. COP31 President Murat Kurum said the draft was not adopted because there was no consensus, and added, as quoted by CBS, "we did not impose this text on anyone." Al Jazeera reports that the Turkish presidency said no new text would follow and existing decisions would be implemented.

The main dispute was fossil fuels. Al Jazeera reports that the EU refused a text that "does not even mention fossil fuels", a Russian delegate said Russia "cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel", and Saudi Arabia argued for keeping all solutions on the table. CBS News reports that a coalition led by France and Panama, with countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific, rejected the draft as too weak on fossil fuels and climate finance. Panama's Juan Carlos Navarro said, per CBS, "We cannot continue to be held hostage by petroleum producers."

Al Jazeera reports that the rejected draft would have acknowledged that warming is on course to pass 1.5 C, and that its revised version had dropped a 120 billion dollar target for helping poorer countries adapt. Down To Earth reports that a roadmap on moving away from fossil fuels is left to the COP31 and COP32 presidencies, with conclusions due at COP32.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply disappointed" (CBS News, Al Jazeera), and Premium Times reports that Guterres blamed fossil fuel interests and compared their tactics to the tobacco industry's. Australia's Chris Bowen, who led the negotiations, called the collapse "very disappointing" (Al Jazeera) and spoke of "unbridgeable red lines" (CBS News). The United States sent no delegation for the second year, according to CBS News.

Al Jazeera notes that the last UN climate talks to end without an agreement were in Copenhagen in 2009. More than 90 countries signed a separate electrification pledge at the summit, Al Jazeera reports.

stories.title: Protests over living costs and housing ran across Europe on 20 and 21 November, with France holding its sixth weekend of marches in a row.
stories.summary: France's Interior Ministry counted 82,500 marchers nationwide on Saturday, against 150,000 claimed by organisers; Lisbon, Berlin and Italian cities also saw marches and strikes.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera (citing Reuters), ABC News Australia, Denver Gazette, Khaama Press · velocity: weekend event, France's movement still weekly
detail: Al Jazeera reports that France's Interior Ministry counted 82,500 protesters on Saturday 21 November, 21,500 of them in Paris, down from 106,000 the weekend before; organisers claimed 150,000. About 70,000 police and gendarmes were deployed. Reuters, cited by Al Jazeera, reported sporadic violence, including in Marseille, and riot police charged protesters in Paris in the evening. The movement began in September with students demanding better schools; unions and the Yellow Vests have since joined.

In Lisbon, thousands marched in heavy rain behind the CGTP union federation for higher wages and pensions and cheaper housing, Al Jazeera reports. In Italy, the CGIL union held a national strike on Friday 20 November that hit transport, schools and some health services, with marches in more than 100 cities; union leader Maurizio Landini claimed over one million participants, a figure no independent count has confirmed. About 4,000 people rallied in Berlin on Friday as part of a youth strike that organisers said was planned in at least 25 countries.

stories.title: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on 22 November that the US and Canada are "fairly close" to a trade deal, days after a report of a Pentagon memo limiting military ties with Canada.
stories.summary: Greer told Fox News that negotiators have "made a lot of progress" but called Canada's new trade deal with China "a little bit backwards"; separately, Canada's defence minister said Ottawa knew of no restrictions from the reported Hegseth memo.
stories.heat: BNN Bloomberg, CTV News, Newsweek, The Globe and Mail, Washington Post (via Newsweek) · velocity: rising, both strands new on 21 and 22 Nov
detail: BNN Bloomberg reports that Greer said in a Fox News interview on Sunday 22 November that the two countries are "fairly close" and have "made a lot of progress." Talks broke down in August, after which President Trump put 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods and services and Prime Minister Mark Carney answered in September with dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs. Both sides have since returned to the table. Greer said Canada's new trade agreement with China, signed on 17 November with tariff concessions on Canadian pork and seafood and relief on Chinese steel and aluminium, moves "a little bit backwards" and raises a concern he called bipartisan.

Separately, the Washington Post reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth circulated a secret memo limiting military contact with Canada; the Post had not seen the memo itself, according to Newsweek. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the guidance does not affect intelligence cooperation, NORAD or NATO cooperation. Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said at the Halifax International Security Forum, "We're not aware of any restrictions" (Newsweek), and four Canadian sources told The Globe and Mail that Ottawa had not been told of the memo.

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for coalition talks on 22 November and agreed to keep talking, with no breakthrough reported.
stories.summary: The two parties called the meeting substantive in a joint statement; Eisenkot has until December to form a government and still rules out serving under Netanyahu.
stories.heat: Haaretz, Ynet, ABC News Australia, France 24, Arab News, Deccan Herald · velocity: steady, talks ongoing
stories.about: Gadi Eisenkot is a former Israeli army chief of staff who leads the Yashar party and holds the mandate to form a government after the October election.
detail: New since yesterday: the first session of the planned "marathon" talks took place. Haaretz reports that Yashar and Likud representatives met on Sunday 22 November and agreed to further talks; Ynet reports a joint statement calling the meeting "substantive" and saying dialogue will continue. Ynet also quotes an opposition source who saw no progress toward a unity government, and reports that the session lasted a little over an hour.

ABC News Australia reports that Likud wants an end to boycotts of Netanyahu and a unity government of parties that accept Israel as the Jewish nation-state, excluding Arab parties, with guidelines that reject Palestinian statehood. Eisenkot is open to a government with Likud members but rules out serving under Netanyahu, and has said that if broad talks fail he will put a minority national emergency government to a parliamentary vote. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett wants a unity government headed by Eisenkot and will not join Netanyahu's bloc, according to France 24. The October election gave neither bloc a clear majority.

stories.title: Spain entered the last week before its 29 November snap election with polls putting the People's Party narrowly ahead of Pedro Sanchez's Socialists.
stories.summary: A 40dB poll for El Pais and Cadena SER had the PP at 31.9% and the PSOE at 31.2%, with the PP and Vox together projected above the 176 seats needed for a majority.
stories.heat: The Olive Press, The Local Spain, Catalan News, QNC News · velocity: rising toward the 29 Nov vote
detail: The Olive Press reports that the 40dB tracker for El Pais and Cadena SER put the PP at 31.9% and the PSOE at 31.2%, a statistical tie, while projecting 189 seats for the PP and Vox together, above the 176 needed in the 350-seat Congress. In the same pollster's survey after the only head-to-head TV debate on 19 November, 43% judged Alberto Nunez Feijoo the winner and 33.3% Sanchez. The debate drew an average audience of more than ten million, and Sanchez apologised in it for corruption cases in his party.

Housing, living costs, immigration and corruption lead the campaign, The Olive Press reports, after housing protests in October and a general strike on 11 November, the first in 14 years. A More in Common poll found 62.9% of left-wing voters named housing as a main problem and 61% of right-wing voters named immigration.

stories.title: At least 24 people died when a boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized in Nigeria's Bayelsa state on 20 November.
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Emergency Management Agency gave the toll on 21 November as search and rescue went on; police had first reported four deaths.
stories.heat: Reuters (via US News and syndicated copies), AFP (via Citizen Digital), Express Tribune · velocity: settled
detail: Reuters-syndicated reports dated 22 November say the crowded boat capsized on Friday 20 November in Bayelsa state in southern Nigeria while carrying people to a funeral. Manzo Ezekiel, a spokesman for the National Emergency Management Agency, said 24 bodies had been recovered by Saturday, Citizen Digital (AFP) reports, and Reuters reports 24 survivors rescued. Police first reported four bodies, including two children, and blamed a mechanical failure. Reuters reports that Governor Douye Diri ordered an investigation, and Citizen Digital reports a statement of sympathy from President Bola Tinubu.

sections.title: Krieg
sections.blurb: NATO chief Rutte says the alliance will defend every inch of Poland after the missile crash, two more tankers are hit off Oman as Iran keeps Hormuz shut, and Iran strikes a civilian plant in Bahrain while the Houthis fire missiles at Riyadh.

stories.title: Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz reached their highest level of the Iran war, as Iran showed a new missile launcher on state TV.
stories.summary: The maritime risk firm Marisks, cited by CNN, says projectiles hit three tankers leaving the strait on 20 and 21 November; Iranian state TV showed a launcher that fires two liquid-fuel missiles at once.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing lead (542 articles across 7 stories on the Iran tanker attacks), CNN, Al Jazeera, AP via Local 10, Khaleej Times · velocity: escalating, new UKMTO incident on 22 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: CNN reported on 22 November that Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are at their highest level since the war began. Citing the maritime risk firm Marisks, CNN said projectiles struck three tankers leaving the strait on Friday and Saturday (20 and 21 November). Marisks said Iranian involvement was "assessed as likely" but did not confirm who fired.

Iranian state TV showed an underground site where the Revolutionary Guards displayed a launcher able to fire two liquid-fuel missiles at once, AP reported (via Local 10, 21 November). The location was not given. AP said the broadcast was meant to answer US statements that the missile program had been destroyed.

Al Jazeera's correspondent counted about 25 tanker incidents in and around the strait since 14 November. UKMTO recorded 263 ships passing through the strait from 12 to 18 November, 15% fewer than the week before, Al Jazeera reported on 22 November.

On the evening of 22 November, UKMTO reported an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman, with no further detail, Khaleej Times reported. Al Jazeera said oil briefly crossed $100 a barrel before settling at $83, and that the IEA puts the war's cumulative loss at 2.8 billion barrels of oil and 60 billion cubic metres of gas from the Gulf.

stories.title: Sea drones hit the Russian navy corvette Merkury at Benghazi in Libya on 22 November, and satellite images show the ship mostly capsized.
stories.summary: Libyan officials told AP the drones came from a Ukrainian-run base in western Libya; Ukraine has not claimed the attack, and a Malta-flagged cargo ship was also hit off Benghazi the same day.
stories.about: The Merkury is a small Russian warship (corvette). Benghazi is held by Libya's eastern-based government, which has a cooperation deal with Russia; western Libya is run by a rival government.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, AP via SCMP, Inquirer and Military.com, The Hill, TWZ, France 24 · velocity: new on 22 Nov, investigation opening
detail: At dawn on Sunday 22 November, sea drones hit the Russian navy corvette Merkury in Benghazi port, causing an explosion and a fire, Libya's eastern-based government said, as reported by Al Jazeera. Satellite imagery from Vantor showed the ship had mostly capsized and sunk, with only its bow visible. Libyan officials said at least four drones were intercepted before two struck the ship (AP, via Military.com).

Unnamed Libyan officials told AP that the drones were launched from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, mainly drone experts based near Misrata. TWZ, citing a Ukrainian source, said Ukraine's SBU security service launched them. Ukraine has made no official claim. Local sources told Al Jazeera an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed; no official toll was given.

The same evening a sea drone hit a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off Benghazi; its crew were rescued with minor injuries, France 24 and Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Osama Hammad of the eastern government asked for a UN investigation and said Libya was "not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war". A joint investigation with Russia has been opened.

stories.title: Arab states and the Arab League condemned a new Iranian attack on Bahrain, which injured two people, one of them a Pakistani resident in critical condition.
stories.summary: Bahrain says an Iranian strike set fire to a civilian industrial site in Sitra; Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim they destroyed two US Patriot radars at the al-Riffa and Awali bases, which has not been confirmed.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, Khaleej Times live, Sunday Guardian · velocity: high on 22 Nov, condemnations through the day
detail: New since yesterday: Khaleej Times reported on 22 November that an Iranian attack in Bahrain injured two people and that a Pakistani resident was in critical condition. The UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt and the Arab League each condemned the attack the same day.

Bahrain said the strike on 21 November hit a civilian industrial facility in Sitra and started a fire, and that it stopped several other attacks, Al Jazeera reported. The Revolutionary Guards said their missile and drone attack on US positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases destroyed two US Patriot radars, in reply to a US strike on a radar site on Iran's Hengam Island. No independent source has confirmed the radar claim.
Iran's army also said it damaged a US F-16 over the Gulf. US Central Command denied it, saying "all US fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for" (Al Jazeera).

stories.title: A Russian drone strike collapsed part of an apartment block in Dymer, north of Kyiv, and Ukrainian rescuers are still searching for people under the rubble.
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service said on 22 November that two people were killed and 11 were missing; other Ukrainian reports later put the toll at three. Zelensky said Russia fired about 2,700 drones in one week.
stories.about: Dymer is a town in the Vyshhorod district of Kyiv region, about 45 km north of Kyiv.
stories.heat: France 24 live, Kyiv Post, Oman Observer, Latin Times, NBC · velocity: rising toll on 22 and 23 Nov
detail: Overnight into 22 November, a Russian drone hit a five-storey apartment block in Dymer and part of it collapsed, Kyiv Post reported. Zelensky said nine residents were evacuated and 14 people were unaccounted for. By the afternoon, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said two people were killed, including an 18-year-old, four were wounded, including a child, and rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children (France 24 live page). Ukrainian outlet ua.news later reported a third body recovered.

Zelensky said Russia launched about 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 aerial bombs and 165 missiles in the past week, and asked the US to approve Patriot missile transfers (France 24). Odesa schools move to remote teaching from 23 to 27 November after damage to the power grid. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X that "Europe cannot afford to respond to each incident in isolation" (Kyiv Post).

Russia's Defence Ministry, via TASS, said it shot down 792 Ukrainian drones in 24 hours and captured Sosnovy Bor in Kharkiv region; France 24 could not verify this. Regional officials in Russia's Krasnodar region said Ukrainian drones injured five people.

stories.title: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels on 23 November about the Russian missiles that fell in Poland, and Poland will present proposals for air defence on the eastern flank.
stories.summary: Lublin prosecutors say the three missiles that fell on 20 November were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles and nobody was hurt; Prime Minister Donald Tusk calls it an intentional provocation.
stories.heat: France 24, NV, Censor.net, Washington Times · velocity: meeting today, outcome not yet reported
detail: New since yesterday: Lublin prosecutors said the three missiles that fell in Poland on Friday 20 November were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles and that no one was injured, France 24 reported on 22 November. Other reports describe two cruise missiles and one jet-powered drone coming down in Podkarpackie and Lublin provinces during Russian attacks on Ukraine (NV).

Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the council meets at NATO headquarters on 23 November; Deputy Defence Minister Pawel Zalewski represents Poland. Censor.net reports that Warsaw will give allies its own assessment of the incident and proposals to strengthen air defence on the eastern flank. Tusk called it "an intentional provocation" by the Kremlin. No outcome had been reported at the time of writing.

stories.title: Trump says Iran fired more missiles and drones last week than at any time in over a year, and that he leans toward new strikes after the new year if talks fail.
stories.summary: Trump wrote on Truth Social on 22 November that US defences shot all of them down; the attack numbers come from Trump only and have no independent confirmation.
stories.heat: Fox News, Israel National News, CBS live, many wire reprints · velocity: new on 22 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: on 22 November Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran had launched more missiles and drones in the past week than at any time in over a year, and that "they've all been knocked down, and done no damage", Fox News reported. Trump linked the rise to the 3 November midterm elections, which Democrats won.

Trump told Fox News he is leaning toward resuming strikes on Iran after the new year if talks fail, and warned that Iranian vessels testing the US naval blockade would be destroyed. CBS earlier reported Trump saying his next move might not come until 2027. No Pentagon figures on the interceptions were found.

stories.title: The Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery on 22 November, while the Saudi-led coalition says it shot down Houthi drones and a missile that day.
stories.summary: The coalition reported two drones, aimed at Riyadh and the southern region, and one missile in the western region; there is no independent confirmation of damage at Rabigh. The exchange follows coalition strikes on Yemen's Hodeidah port from 20 November.
stories.about: Rabigh is a large oil refinery on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, north of Jeddah.
stories.heat: Khaleej Times live, The National, US News (Reuters), Marine Insight · velocity: escalating since the coalition's Hodeidah strikes on 20 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: the Houthis said at about 22:00 on 22 November that they attacked the Rabigh refinery, Khaleej Times reported. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi drone heading for Riyadh, a second drone launched toward the southern region and a missile over the western region the same day. Neither side's claims have been independently confirmed.

The coalition struck Hodeidah port on 20 November, saying it hit facilities "used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles", after telling civilians to leave, The National reported. The UN warned the same day that escalation could threaten humanitarian supply routes. The Houthi-run al-Masirah TV said Saudi warplanes struck Hodeidah again on the evening of 21 November; that report comes from the Houthi side only.

Earlier, on 19 November, Saudi Civil Defense said a Houthi attack damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh and nearby buildings, with no injuries, The National reported. Reuters sources said a missile hit the tower directly, while the coalition first blamed falling debris from an intercepted missile.
Marine Insight reported that the Houthis had warned Saudi Red Sea port workers to leave and threatened Jeddah and other ports if coalition strikes on Hodeidah continue.

stories.title: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II was still burning in the Gulf of Finland on 22 November, and Finland says the war is spilling over.
stories.summary: Finland's coast guard said the 16 crew were moved to a Russian ship; Kaliningrad sounded its first air alert since February 2022 over a suspicious object from Lithuania.
stories.heat: France 24 live · velocity: follow-up of the 21 Nov drone hit
detail: New since yesterday: Finland's coast guard said the Sparta II, hit by drones on Saturday 21 November, was still on fire on 22 November and that its 16 crew had been moved to a nearby Russian ship, France 24 reported. Finland said the war was "spilling over".

Kaliningrad governor Alexei Bezprozvannykh said a "suspicious object" from Lithuania set off an air alert in the Nemansky district; local media said it was the first siren there since 24 February 2022. AP could not verify drone images near Baltiysk (France 24).

stories.title: Drone strikes on Khartoum killed at least four civilians on 22 November and damaged a UN building, according to local reports and the UN.
stories.summary: The Rapid Support Forces were blamed; Sudan's army says the drones were launched from Ethiopia, which Ethiopia denies.
stories.heat: ABC News (Australia) · velocity: single-day event, one major outlet
detail: Drone strikes on Khartoum on Sunday 22 November killed at least four civilians and injured at least nine, according to local reports cited by ABC News on 23 November. Air defences fired at drones that appeared to target government buildings and the airport. A UN statement said a UN building was damaged.

The Rapid Support Forces were blamed. The Sudanese army said the drones came from Ethiopia; Addis Ababa denies allowing attacks from its territory. ABC cites a UN report that drone attacks killed more than 1,630 civilians in Sudan from January to October 2026.

stories.title: Fighting near a hospital in Ituri, eastern DR Congo, trapped health workers for over 24 hours and disrupted the Ebola response, WHO chief Tedros said on 22 November.
stories.summary: Staff sheltered in a maternity ward while WHO sought a safe way out; separately, an M23-linked group claims it shot down a Congolese army jet in South Kivu, which is not confirmed.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, The Observer (Uganda), Archyde · velocity: new on 22 Nov
detail: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Sunday 22 November that heavy clashes near a hospital in Ituri province had kept staff in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours and put "patients, families and health workers at grave risk", Al Jazeera reported. Al Jazeera did not say who was fighting. WHO counted 11,613 Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths in DR Congo as of 17 November.

Earlier this month, AFP reported (via The Standard, 13 November) that fighters of the Islamic State-linked ADF killed at least 44 civilians in raids on villages in Ituri's Mambasa territory in the week to 13 November, days after an ADF attack in North Kivu that killed 66 people.
In South Kivu, an M23-linked group claimed it shot down a Congolese army fighter jet over Minembwe on 22 November, The Observer reported; there is no independent confirmation.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Toxic liquor kills at least 11 in Manipur, Pant's century puts India far ahead in Wellington, Nepal's PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi, and the Nitish Setu opening turns into a naming row.

stories.title: India need five more New Zealand wickets on the last day of the Wellington Test, with New Zealand 190 for 5 and still 162 runs behind.
stories.summary: India declared at 720 for 9, the highest Test total ever made in New Zealand, and took two wickets in the morning session of day five; the result is not yet known.
stories.heat: Tribune, Outlook India, ABC News, Cricket World, Crex live score · velocity: live, final day in progress (new: day five play)
detail: New since yesterday: day five play. New Zealand resumed on 119 for 2 and reached 157 for 4 at lunch, 195 behind, The Tribune reported. Devon Conway was out for 65, caught by Rishabh Pant off Washington Sundar, and Rachin Ravindra for 37, caught by KL Rahul off Prasidh Krishna.

In the second session the Crex live score showed New Zealand on 190 for 5 after 83.2 overs, trailing by 162, with Daryl Mitchell on 24 and Glenn Phillips on 3. No result had been reported when this edition was written.

India declared their first innings at 720 for 9 in 166 overs on day four, a 352-run lead. ABC News reported it as the highest team total in a Test in New Zealand. Pant scored 128 off 153 balls, his ninth Test century, and KL Rahul scored 136. New Zealand had been all out for 368, with Henry Nicholls 175 not out; Jasprit Bumrah took 4 for 92.

stories.title: The toll from spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel district has risen to at least 16 dead, with about 600 people treated in hospital and six people arrested.
stories.summary: Manipur Police say the liquor came from Sugnu in Kakching district; a government panel has one month to report, and lab tests on the cause are pending.
stories.heat: ThePrint, Organiser, Daily Jagran, Statesman, NE Now, Tech Times and others · velocity: rising toll, 21 and 22 Nov (new: higher toll, arrests, inquiry)
stories.about: Chandel is a district in southern Manipur on the Myanmar border. Sugnu is a town in neighbouring Kakching district.
detail: New since yesterday: the toll and the arrests. Manipur Police said at least 16 people have died and about 600 have been in hospital since 18 November after drinking suspected spurious liquor, ThePrint and Daily Jagran reported. Three of the deaths happened on Saturday 21 November. The Statesman reported 17 deaths on Sunday, with 230 people still in hospital and 38 on dialysis; that figure was not confirmed elsewhere.

Police arrested six people from Kakching district for stocking, buying and selling the liquor, seized 2,419 litres of illicit liquor and registered 48 cases since 17 November, Organiser reported. Police think the liquor was bought in Sugnu, not made in Chandel.

Excise Commissioner Hungyo Worshang said a committee will report within one month, NE Now reported. Doctors suspect methanol poisoning, but no lab result has confirmed it; samples went to the Forensic Science Laboratory. Congress has demanded accountability.

stories.title: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah meets Modi at Hyderabad House at 11 am today, and the two are due to sign agreements and launch the Janakpurdham-Ayodhya train.
stories.summary: S Jaishankar called on Shah in Delhi on 22 November; air routes and a proposed development package are expected to be the main issues.
stories.heat: Himal Press, Deccan Herald, OnlineKhabar, Free Press Journal, The Wire, Kathmandu Post · velocity: rising, talks today (new: arrival, Jaishankar meeting, full schedule)
detail: New since yesterday: Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday 22 November for a two-day state visit, his first bilateral trip abroad, and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called on Shah at Hotel Taj, Himal Press reported.

The schedule for Monday 23 November, per Himal Press: a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan, a visit to Rajghat, a one-on-one meeting with Modi at Hyderabad House at 11 am, delegation-level talks, a joint virtual launch of the Janakpurdham-Ayodhya railway service, the signing of agreements, a lunch hosted by Modi, a call on President Droupadi Murmu, and departure at 5 pm.

Deccan Herald listed new air routes and economic aid on the agenda. The Wire said airspace access is the key issue for Nepal. The weekly Janakpur-Ayodhya service was approved by Indian Railways in mid-November, Kathmandu Post reported. Outcomes were not known when this edition was written.

stories.title: India's food regulator FSSAI has ordered the prosecution of Bisleri International after a sample of its packaged drinking water was declared unsafe.
stories.summary: The first test found bromate over the limit, and a referral lab then found polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons; no recall has been announced.
stories.heat: Ground News 19 sources (47% right-leaning) · ThePrint, India TV, Gulf News, Law Chakra · velocity: rising, 22 Nov
detail: FSSAI said a regulatory sample of Bisleri's packaged drinking water (not mineral water) failed the bromate limits and was declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, India TV and ThePrint reported on 22 November.

Bisleri appealed, and the sample went to a referral food laboratory, which also declared it unsafe because it found polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons. FSSAI said the findings established violations relating to unsafe food. Gulf News reported that the announcement did not mention a recall or licence action. Which batch or plant the sample came from was not reported.

stories.title: Tata Sons has postponed its 26 November board meeting after Noel Tata said directors received the agenda only four days ahead.
stories.summary: Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, had asked the board to vote on a restructuring to avoid an RBI-required listing and a Rs 25,000 crore buyback of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group's stake; no new date is known.
stories.heat: NewsBytes (postponement, 23 Nov) · Moneylife, Business Standard, The Statesman on the agenda · velocity: rising (new: postponement)
detail: New since yesterday: NewsBytes reported on 23 November that Tata Sons will delay the board meeting set for 26 November. Noel Tata told the company secretary and the chairman that directors got the agenda four days ahead, less than the seven days required. No new date was reported. Only one outlet has reported the postponement so far.

Noel Tata had asked for two items, Moneylife and The Statesman reported: a reorganisation of Tata Sons so that it does not have to list under Reserve Bank of India rules, and a selective capital reduction in which Tata Sons buys back the Shapoorji Pallonji Group's stake for a gross Rs 25,000 crore.

stories.title: Two Indian Army soldiers died when a tank ran over them during a training exercise near Hisar in Haryana.
stories.summary: Ground News flags this as a Blindspot: of its 11 sources, 67% lean right and 17% lean left.
stories.heat: Ground News 11 sources, Blindspot (left 17%, center 16%, right 67%) · Tribune, ETV Bharat, India.com, Kalinga TV · velocity: settled, 21-22 Nov
detail: The Tribune and ETV Bharat reported that two Army non-commissioned officers, both from Uttar Pradesh, were run over by a tank near Bhojraj village in Hisar district during a routine exercise in which about 32 tanks took part. Both were declared dead at the Hisar Military Hospital.

Reports differ on the cause: one says the driver could not see the soldiers in time, another blames dust raised by the exercise. Reports also differ on the date (21 or 22 November). Hisar Police started legal proceedings and a post-mortem was done.

stories.title: Modi told Gujarat BJP workers that 50 crore Indians have left poverty and that some people still hesitate to acknowledge it.
stories.summary: He cited a World Bank report saying extreme poverty fell from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023, and credited his government's schemes.
stories.heat: Ground News 5 sources (60% right-leaning) · Business Standard, ETV Bharat, Millennium Post, Daily Pioneer, News24 · velocity: settled, 22 Nov
detail: Modi spoke virtually on Sunday 22 November to the post-Diwali Sneh Milan meetings held in all 182 Gujarat assembly constituencies, Business Standard reported. He cited a World Bank report that about 50 crore (500 million) Indians have been lifted out of poverty, with extreme poverty falling from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023.

He recalled that critics had doubted bank accounts and LPG connections for the poor and said those schemes drove the change. Daily Pioneer framed the speech as a claim that only the BJP had done it. No opposition response was found.

stories.title: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has joined the BJP and was named a special invitee to the national executive of the party's OBC Morcha.
stories.summary: The BJP announced the appointment on 21 November; no constituency or election role has been reported.
stories.heat: Gujarat Samachar, Khel Now, CricToday, SportsTiger · velocity: settled, 21-22 Nov
detail: Chahal met Amar Pal Maurya, the OBC Morcha national president and a Rajya Sabha member, in Delhi before the announcement on Saturday 21 November, Khel Now and Gujarat Samachar reported. On X, Chahal thanked Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and Maurya.
One outlet said Chahal was named as a special invitee from Delhi. The reports do not mention a seat or an election role.

stories.title: Seven members of Army families died in a car-truck crash in Gujarat's Kutch, and at least nine people died in a separate crash in Rajasthan's Kota.
stories.summary: Modi announced Rs 2 lakh for each dead person's family and Rs 50,000 for each injured person in both crashes.
stories.heat: ANI, Deccan Chronicle, Zee Business, Asianet Newsable, Dainik Jagran · velocity: settled, 21-22 Nov
detail: In Kutch, a car hit a truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway near Vekariya Rann on Saturday night, 21 November, police said. Seven people died, including three children and two women. Reports say they were relatives of Army personnel from Garhwal in Uttarakhand, returning from a Rann of Kutch trip. ANI quoted police as saying the car was trying to overtake.

Modi also expressed grief over a crash in Kota district that killed at least nine people. On 22 November he announced Rs 2 lakh from the PM's National Relief Fund for each dead person's next of kin and Rs 50,000 for each injured person, for both crashes.

stories.title: Indian and Chinese Army commanders have held a second round of talks on easing tension along the border in Arunachal Pradesh.
stories.summary: The closed-door talks began on 8 November and ran for about ten days; no outcome has been published.
stories.heat: The Federal, Madhyamam, Bombay Samachar, Press News Agency, Dainik Jagran daily digest (22 Nov) · velocity: settled
detail: Lt Gen Girish Kalia, who commands the Army's III Corps, led the Indian side, and an External Affairs Ministry official attended, the reports say. The talks covered rules of engagement, reducing friction between patrols, keeping communication channels open and calming tension before winter.

The first round in the eastern sector was held on 6 and 7 September at Kibithoo, after tension at Taksing in Upper Subansiri district. One outlet called the talks cordial. No official readout or agreement text has been found.

stories.title: Delhi's air stayed in the 'poor' range on 22 November, with an average AQI of about 239, and Gurgaon recorded the season's first single-digit low of 7.3 degrees.
stories.summary: Eight monitoring stations were in the 'very poor' range; the 'very poor' city-wide forecast for Sunday did not happen.
stories.heat: Outlook India, The Chenab Times, Dainik Jagran daily digest · velocity: steady (new: Sunday reading)
detail: New since yesterday: the Sunday reading. The Chenab Times reported an AQI of 239 on 22 November, in the 'poor' range, with eight stations 'very poor' and 12 'moderate'. Outlook India reported 237 at 6 am and readings of 237 to 270 through the day, with DTU the worst station at 362.
Forecasters had expected 'very poor' air on Sunday; the city average stayed 'poor'. Gurgaon recorded 7.3 degrees, the first single-digit minimum of the season, a Dainik Jagran digest reported.

sections.title: Cinema
sections.blurb: Sunrise on the Reaping heads for about $120 million, Ramayana Part 1 passes Rs 900 crore net in India, O.M: Operation Mole holds on day 2, a Home Alone sequel with Macaulay Culkin is in early works, and a film workers' body asks for protection for Saif Ali Khan and the Bachchans.

stories.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to an estimated $120 million in North America and $225 million worldwide, by Sunday studio estimates.
stories.summary: The sixth Hunger Games film beat pre-release forecasts of $80 million or more, earned an A- CinemaScore and was the fifth $100 million domestic opening of 2026, AP reports.
stories.heat: Deadline, Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, AP, Boxoffice Pro, IndieWire · velocity: peaked, Sunday estimates in, Monday actuals pending (new: weekend estimates; Saturday projection ran 22 Nov)
detail: New since yesterday: the Sunday studio estimates. The film took an estimated $120 million from 4,018 North American theatres over 20 to 22 November, AP and The Hollywood Reporter report, plus $105 million from 84 international territories for a $225 million global start, per Variety. Boxoffice Pro lists the days as Friday $56 million (including $21.25 million in previews), Saturday $36.3 million and Sunday $27.7 million.

Deadline reported in early November that presales were ahead of Wicked's and set an $80 million-plus floor. Deadline's Sunday headline calls the result the fourth-best opening in the series; The Hollywood Reporter says it is the fifth-biggest opening in Lionsgate's history.

AP gives a budget of about $150 million and reports that 74% of the audience was aged 18 to 34 and 67% was female. The CinemaScore was A-, up from B+ for The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes (2023), which grossed $361.8 million worldwide. Reviews were 67% positive on Rotten Tomatoes.

AP says many potential viewers stayed home to play Grand Theft Auto VI the same weekend. Overall ticket sales were about 10% below the same weekend in 2025, when Wicked: For Good opened. Lionsgate film chairman Adam Fogelson told AP that it is not common for a sixth film to completely reverse a franchise's trajectory. Final figures are due on Monday 23 November.

stories.title: Ramayana Part 1 took about Rs 79 crore net in India over its third weekend, for an 18-day India total of Rs 942.75 crore, by Sacnilk's count.
stories.summary: Sacnilk puts the third Sunday at Rs 35.60 crore net and the worldwide gross at about Rs 1,693.50 crore, though its own summary box shows a lower figure.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, Koimoi, Pinkvilla, Bollywood Hungama, Zee Business, Outlook India · velocity: still climbing, third-Monday advance sales tracked (new: third Sunday and weekend total; third Saturday ran 22 Nov)
detail: New since yesterday: the third Sunday and the weekend total. Sacnilk estimates Rs 35.60 crore net in India on Day 18 (Sunday 22 November), up 28.8% from Saturday's Rs 27.65 crore. Hindi gave Rs 26.25 crore, Malayalam Rs 3.40 crore, Kannada Rs 2.50 crore, Tamil Rs 2.40 crore and Telugu Rs 1.05 crore, with 37.9% overall occupancy across 16,277 shows.

Sacnilk's 18-day India net total is Rs 942.75 crore, and the third weekend (Days 16 to 18) added about Rs 79 crore. Its article gives overseas at Rs 567 crore and a worldwide gross of Rs 1,693.50 crore, while the page's summary box still lists Rs 1,651 crore to Day 17. Zee Business reports the film has crossed Rs 1,650 crore worldwide.

Koimoi's figures differ slightly: Rs 27.18 crore for the third Saturday and a worldwide gross of about Rs 1,612.54 crore after 16 days. Before Sunday, Koimoi noted that Dhurandhar's Rs 40.3 crore is the highest third-Sunday figure; Sacnilk's estimate leaves Ramayana below it. Bollywood Hungama reported third-Monday advance sales of Rs 3.58 crore from 1.59 lakh tickets.

stories.title: A new Avengers: Doomsday trailer may arrive on Monday 23 November, going by a remark from Hayley Atwell; Marvel has not confirmed a date.
stories.summary: Joe Russo told the Doha Film Festival only to keep refreshing feeds before the film opens on 18 December, Screen Daily and Deadline report.
stories.heat: Deadline, Screen Daily, Inquisitr, Cosmic Book News and other fan sites · velocity: rising, expected today
detail: Hayley Atwell reportedly said at the stage door after a Broadway performance of Much Ado About Nothing on 20 November that the trailer comes out on Monday and that it is amazing, according to several entertainment sites. Marvel Studios has not announced a time.

At the Doha Film Festival, Joe Russo gave no date. Screen Daily quotes him saying that between now and the film's 18 December release fans should keep checking and keep refreshing their feeds. Earlier rumours of a trailer on 16 or 18 November did not come true. Disney has separately announced a Doomsday sneak peek for 30 November during an ABC holiday special. The Monday date rests on Atwell's remark alone.

stories.title: Dhanush's O.M: Operation Mole crossed Rs 50 crore net in India in its first weekend, by Sacnilk's count, with about Rs 85 crore gross worldwide.
stories.summary: Sacnilk estimates Rs 15.90 crore net on Sunday, a 2.2% dip from Saturday, for a three-day India total of Rs 50.25 crore.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, Pinkvilla, NewsBytes, ETV Bharat · velocity: settling after opening weekend (new: Sunday and weekend totals; Day 2 ran 22 Nov)
stories.about: O.M: Operation Mole (listed by Sacnilk as O.M Chapter 1) is a Tamil action thriller directed by Rajkumar Periasamy, starring Dhanush, Mammootty and Sai Pallavi, released in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi on 20 November.
detail: New since yesterday: the first Sunday and weekend total. Sacnilk estimates Rs 15.90 crore net in India on Day 3 (Sunday 22 November): Rs 11.55 crore in Tamil, Rs 3.80 crore in Telugu and Rs 55 lakh in Hindi, from 6,546 shows. That is 2.2% below Saturday's Rs 16.25 crore.

Sacnilk's three-day India total is Rs 50.25 crore net (Rs 58.30 crore gross), and with Rs 27 crore gross overseas the worldwide gross is Rs 85.30 crore. NewsBytes reports a Rs 49.57 crore net weekend and calls it Dhanush's biggest opening; trackers' daily figures differ by about Rs 1 to 3 crore. Sacnilk's Day 1 page lists Rs 18.10 crore net.

stories.title: David Fincher defended using AI after critics said The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth shows signs of generative AI imagery.
stories.summary: Fincher told the Los Angeles Times that he is not a Luddite and asked, of AI, "Well, it exists. Should we not use it?" The Netflix film opens in IMAX over Thanksgiving.
stories.heat: Deadline, TheWrap, Yahoo, Futurism · velocity: steady, film opens this week
stories.about: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is a Netflix film directed by David Fincher from a script by Quentin Tarantino, with Brad Pitt returning as the stuntman from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.
detail: Some critics and viewers said the film contains generative AI imagery; one critic called it "blatant and egregious". The reviews did not name specific scenes, and no one involved has confirmed which shots, if any, used generative AI, according to TheWrap and Yahoo.

In a Los Angeles Times interview reported by Deadline (first published 20 November), Fincher said of AI: "Well, it exists. Should we not use it?" Bloomberg reported in March that he was using post-production tools from InterPositive, the AI company founded by Ben Affleck. AP lists the film among Thanksgiving weekend releases in IMAX.

stories.title: Kartik Aaryan will star in Kaaliya, a monster thriller from Dharma Productions and his new banner Dopamine Studios, due in cinemas on 5 May 2028.
stories.summary: The film was announced on 22 November, Kartik Aaryan's birthday, with Sandeep Modi directing, Bollywood Hungama reports.
stories.heat: Bollywood Hungama, Koimoi, Sacnilk, ETV Bharat, India.com · velocity: new, announced 22 Nov
detail: Bollywood Hungama reports that Kaaliya draws on the mythology and folklore of the Indian heartland; the announcement glimpse shows a mother telling her son the story of a monster named Kaaliya. No plot was given.

Sandeep Modi, who made the series The Night Manager and Aarya, directs; it is his first Hindi theatrical release. The producers are Karan Johar, Adar Poonawalla, Apoorva Mehta, Somen Mishra, Marijke deSouza and Kartik Aaryan, and Dharma will release it worldwide. ETV Bharat reports the film marks Kartik Aaryan's move into production with Dopamine Studios.

stories.title: The trailer for Shah Rukh Khan's King will reportedly release on 14 December, ten days before the film opens on 24 December; the makers have not confirmed the trailer date.
stories.summary: Variety India is cited as the source of the trailer date; Red Chillies Entertainment announced the 24 December release earlier.
stories.heat: Variety India (via NewsBytes, Patrika, TrackTollywood, Filmibeat) · velocity: fresh report
detail: NewsBytes, Patrika and TrackTollywood report that the King trailer will come out on 14 December, citing Variety India; Patrika says the makers have not confirmed it. The release date of 24 December was announced by Red Chillies Entertainment.

Siddharth Anand directs the action thriller, which also stars Deepika Padukone, Shah Rukh Khan's sixth film with her, and Suhana Khan. Patrika notes it is Shah Rukh Khan's first release since Dunki in 2023. Avengers: Doomsday opens on 18 December.

stories.title: Sooraj Barjatya's Yeh Prem Mol Liya, with Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari, and Aditya Datt's Gunmaaster G9, with Emraan Hashmi, both open on 27 November.
stories.summary: They are the next Hindi releases against Ramayana's fourth week; both trailers are out.
stories.heat: Outlook India, India TV, Bollywood Hungama, The Hollywood Reporter India, India.com · velocity: building toward Friday
detail: Yeh Prem Mol Liya's trailer launched in Mumbai on 18 November, India TV reports. It runs about 3 minutes 45 seconds and shows the husband, played by Ayushmann Khurrana, moving into the home of the wife, played by Sharvari. Rajshri Productions makes it with Mahaveer Jain Films.

Gunmaaster G9 stars Emraan Hashmi as a dairy farmer who turns vigilante, with Genelia Deshmukh and Aparshakti Khurana, The Hollywood Reporter India and India.com report. Its trailer came out about 11 November and the CBFC gave it an A certificate. PEN Marudhar distributes in India.

stories.title: Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky came second at the US box office with an estimated $9.3 million in its first wide weekend, and audiences gave it an A+ CinemaScore.
stories.summary: The Amazon MGM film about the making of Rocky played 2,477 locations, AP reports; JoBlo says many had expected about twice that.
stories.heat: AP, JoBlo, The Numbers · velocity: settled
detail: AP's Sunday estimates put I Play Rocky at $9.3 million, behind Sunrise on the Reaping. It had opened in seven theatres on 6 November. Paramount's Ebenezer, with Johnny Depp, was third at $7.7 million in its second weekend, down 60%, for $32.5 million domestic. The Cat in the Hat was fourth at $6.9 million and Godzilla Minus Zero fifth at $2.7 million.
Thanksgiving week brings Universal's Focker in Law, Disney's animated Hexed, Netflix's The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in IMAX and Neon's Paper Tiger, AP reports.

stories.title: Former Netflix film executive Tendo Nagenda will become president of Proximity Media, the company founded by Ryan Coogler, Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian, on 30 November.
stories.summary: Nagenda will run creative development and production across film, TV and nonfiction, Variety and IndieWire report.
stories.heat: Variety, IndieWire, TheWrap, C21 Media · velocity: announced about 19 Nov, fading
detail: Nagenda was Netflix's vice president of original film from 2018 to 2022 and then founded 10 by Ten Entertainment, C21 Media reports. Proximity's slate includes the Hulu X-Files series and Marvel's Black Panther 3, and it signed a multi-year deal with Netflix about five months ago.
